objective: Develop FusionBench as a controlled benchmark for improving OKAPI tree search and generalization. Measure search error against exact optima in stated finite tree families or known achievable trees, and measure overfitting on independent data. Every OKAPI experiment compares against three inexpensive baselines on matched predictions and labeled rows: unweighted arithmetic averaging over all providers, ranked-prefix Top-N averaging with N learned on development data, and regularized logistic stacking. Freeze all three before evaluation. Track fit, validation, IID and shifted test losses, variation across data and search seeds, complexity and search cost. Distinguish the ability to represent a logistic stacker from fitting its parameters and from outperforming it on independent data. Compare optional parameter fitting and nonlinear search on both stacking-favorable and interaction-favorable scenarios. Use the literature to identify falsifiable comparisons. Iterate on independent confirmations and counterexamples. Use research/ensemble-mechanisms-stability in FusionBench and research/okapi-algorithm-lab for algorithm development in OKAPI. Publication on PyPI, a paper and integration into dev/main are deferred.
